name: Observation of Υ, Υ′ and Υ″ at the Cornell Electron Storage Ring
notes: The title on the APS page is in TeX markup; it is given here in Unicode (Υ, Υ′, Υ″).

summary.plain: In 1980 the CUSB experiment at Cornell's CESR ring reported the Upsilon family of bound states of a bottom quark and antiquark, seen as narrow peaks in the rate of electron-positron collisions that make hadrons. The data came from a Columbia-Stony Brook sodium iodide detector.
summary.technical: CUSB: the Υ, Υ′ and Υ″ observed as narrow peaks in σ(e⁺e⁻ → hadrons) versus beam energy, using the Columbia University-Stony Brook segmented NaI detector with an integrated luminosity of 1000 nb⁻¹ (Phys. Rev. Lett. 44, 1111, 1980).

title: Observation of Υ, Υ′ and Υ″ at the Cornell Electron Storage Ring
why_it_matters: Berkelman notes that the CUSB experiment provided confirmation of the CLEO measurements of the Υ states at CESR.
